items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Had a lady on the piano, Ted Williams' wife, Irene her name was, and she the one supposed to have the little outfit, see.

ctx.x: Was this the same band that made the recordings?

No, no. Every time they make recordings, it's a couple of different bands, you know. One place I worked, I never did get to tell you, where I was doing very good, a place they called it the Bookstore, on 35th Street. It would open say twelve o'clock at night, and catch all the performance from all nightclubs and things, see. They called it the Bookstore, but they sold, you know, whisking stuff and things like that. But they did sell books in the front, and we had a little four piece outfit in there, and we just…
What was the name of the club that Huey Swift was in?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: So she heard about me, she come and got me to play at the bookstore.

ctx.x: You never know when a Chinaman died? That's what I heard. It's disappeared, huh? Mm-hmm. Do you remember Junie Cobb?

That's the man who got me the job at Jeffrey Tabin. Two brothers, Junie Cobb and Jimmy Cobb. I was playing after, this was before I went to Golden Lily though, I just went to Chicago with the show, Mac and Mac. And we was playing at a little place called Bookstore. I tell you, her wife was playing the piano. Uh, what did this boy play so much piano? Played with us a long time. Tenny Wilson. Tenny Wilson. He had a little girl named Aurene, who was his wife. Good piano player. So she heard about me, she come and…
Law grab her and went in there and got all that stuff out of front of them. Yeah, Gene Carver got me a great job.
